newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on post-high profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on post-high profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday as investors continued to take profits following the market's ascent to a 19-month high on Saturday, brokers said.
The weighted index ended down 35.51 points or 0.54 percent at 6,584.91.
Turnover was a modest T$37.83 billion, the smallest since October 1, indicating market caution.
The index had climbed to 6,644.66 on Saturday, its highest close since 6,650.29 on February 18, 1995.
"The market is effectively entering a consolidation phase after the peak," said Oliver Fang of National Securities.
"The fall was not triggered by a change in the fundamentals. The market simply has a way of forming a psychological barrier every time it hits a peak," Fang said.

The food sector dropped 1.21 percent, pulled lower mainly by news that President Securities, a unit of President Enterprises, faced a government inquiry into possible insider trading and that President Chain Store, another President subsidiary, had delayed its public share offering.
President Enterprises, which had planned on Tuesday to release T$2 billion in President Chain Store shares, fell by 3.47 percent or T$1.50 to close at T$41.70.
The heavily weighted financials suffered mainly from profit-taking, dropping by 0.74 percent.
Brokers expected sentiment to remain stable despite Tuesday's loss, due partly to recent soaring gains on Wall Street that should bode well for the domestic market.
"I don't see the index falling below 6,500 in this wave of profit-taking," Fang said.
A range of 6,550 to 6,620 was seen for Wednesday.
